Definition: Type 1 manager that identifies, designs, and implements deterministic tools for repeatable LLM-independent operations.
A tool that executes without LLM reasoning or mediation.
Classification that separates deterministic tool territory from non-deterministic agent territory.
A deterministic tool that renders valid INIT-TASK briefs for complex or format-sensitive skill dispatch interfaces.
The documented dispatch shape rendered by brief-builder tools from runtime parameters and canonical templates.
Path where tools are written; the default is {REPO_ROOT}/tools/.
Parameter identifying which tool categories to create or update.
Parameter containing paths to agent instruction files to analyze for tool candidates.
Parameter containing an example execution root to inspect for patterns.
Index of tools with name, category, language, purpose, inputs, outputs, and example invocation.
Tool category for folder creation, file creation, template instantiation, and workspace structure.
Tool category for file finding, counting, and field extraction.
Tool category for correctness checks such as schema, enum, coverage, ID format, and referential integrity checks.
Tool territory for CSV merges, group-by sums, pivots, duplicate detection, and conflict detection.
Tool territory for adjacency lists, cycle detection, topological sort, node degrees, orphans, and bidirectional pairs.
Tool territory for filesystem-state JSON, INDEX.md generation, and Run_Context.md generation.
Work requiring interpretation, judgment, content generation, synthesis, assessment, extraction from prose, or orchestration.
Owner of skill design, governance, and the skill subsystem; integrates deterministic helpers into skill contracts.
Tool index used to discover existing tools, avoid duplication, and register compliant tools.
Template structure for shell tools, including shebang, usage, inputs, outputs, input validation, core logic, and output sections.
